haiku-low.q1: After pre-flight checks, before any new release starts (step 4). The live (old) release must keep working on the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Never. Pre-flight check (a) rejects any DROP, RENAME, column type change, or NOT NULL added to an existing column; migrations must be additive.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 new instances need 3 consecutive /healthz passes and a passing smoke suite before the switch, within 10 minutes of T0, else abort.
haiku-low.q4: In one step: step 10 makes one API call setting the public listener's default action to the new target group, moving all traffic at once.
haiku-low.q5: 5xx rate above 1% in a window, zero healthy new targets twice, or 5 minutes without metrics. Listener repoints to old colour; migrations stay.
haiku-low.q6: 30 minutes after the switch until shutdown_due_at. After that, an engineer runs manual rollback R2, redeploying the previous release tag from the existing image.
haiku-low.q7: Applied migrations stay; the failed one's transaction rolls back. No new release starts, live colour keeps serving, deploy marked migration_failed, lock released, alert sent.
haiku-low.q8: Listener's default action shows live target group; DynamoDB state item (environment=catalog-web) records colours and releases. Both must agree; idle colour gets the new release.
haiku-low.q9: A conditional write sets lock_owner on the state item. Held from step 2 to promote or abort; queued deploys wait until old colour shuts down.
haiku-low.q10: Health checks and smoke tests go straight to each idle instance's private address, not the listener, so the new release gets no user traffic before the switch.
haiku-low.q11: Pipeline runs the migration tool once (step 4), never the app at startup. PostgreSQL's migration table records applied migrations, so re-runs skip them.
haiku-low.q12: Aborts: idle instances are stopped, so the next deploy starts clean. Rollbacks: failed colour idles 30 minutes for diagnosis, then stops before the queue resumes.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after pre-flight checks and before the new release starts on the idle colour; migrations run once. The live (old) release must keep working on the migrated database, which is why they must be additive.
sonnet.q2: NOT STATED as allowed. The document only says non-additive changes (drop, rename, type change, NOT NULL on an existing column) are rejected by pre-flight check 3(a). It gives no procedure for when they may be done.
sonnet.q3: All 4 instances must pass the /healthz gate (3 passes in a row each) and the smoke test suite must pass, both by T0 + 10 min. If not, procedure A runs: the listener is untouched, the idle instances are stopped, the state is set to aborted, the lock is released and an alert is sent.
sonnet.q4: At step 10, one API call sets the public listener's default action to forward to the new target group. All traffic moves at once, and the run reads the listener back to confirm.
sonnet.q5: Triggers: 5xx rate strictly above 1% in any window, zero healthy targets in the new target group for 2 consecutive checks, or no metric data for 5 minutes. A zero-request window only alerts. Rollback repoints the listener's default action to the old target group. It sets status to rolled_back, records the reason and readings, and keeps the failed colour running idle with a shutdown time of now + 30 min. The old colour becomes live with no shutdown timer. Migrations are not reversed.
sonnet.q6: Up to 30 minutes after the switch (shutdown_due_at = Ts + 30 min), during retention. After that the old colour is shut down. A problem found later is handled by manual rollback R2: run steps 1 to 12 for the previous release tag, reusing the image already in the registry.
sonnet.q7: The failed migration's transaction rolls back. Migrations that already applied stay in place and are additive, so they are harmless. The run stops, no new release is started, and the live colour keeps serving. The deploy is marked migration_failed, the lock is released and an alert is sent. A failed concurrent index build leaves an invalid index, fixed with a later migration.
sonnet.q8: The pipeline reads the public listener's default action (traffic truth) and the state item (intent truth) at step 2 and checks they agree. The new release goes to the idle colour, the one the listener does not forward to. It is recorded in the DynamoDB state item (environment=catalog-web in catalog-web-deploy), which holds live and idle colour. Step 9 writes previous_live_tg and new_tg.
sonnet.q9: The deploy lock, a conditional write on the state item setting lock_owner, plus the queue. A retention window also blocks new deploys. The lock is released at step 12 (promote), or on abort or failure. Queued deploys still wait until step 13 stops the non-live colour, and step 14 then releases the queue.
sonnet.q10: They go straight to each idle instance's private address, not through the listener. The idle target group is never on the listener before the switch.
sonnet.q11: The deploy pipeline runs the migration tool once at step 4 against the shared database. Schema history in the migration tool's own PostgreSQL table records each migration as applied, so a re-run skips those already applied. The deploy lock allows only one deploy at a time. The app never runs migrations on startup.
sonnet.q12: After an abort (procedure A), the idle instances are deregistered and stopped, so the idle colour is empty and the next deploy starts clean. After a rollback, the failed colour stays running and idle for diagnosis for 30 minutes, then step 13 stops it. The queued deploy starts only after that (step 14). Step 5 also clears any leftovers on the idle colour before starting.
